hints: Apply Newton's second law along the horizontal direction: $D - R = ma$.
Substitute mass $m = 900\text{ kg}$, resistance $R = 350\text{ N}$, and acceleration $a = 0.25\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Calculate $D = 350 + 900(0.25)$ to obtain the driving force.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law along the horizontal road:
$$D - R = ma$$
$$D - 350 = 900 \times 0.25 = 225$$
$$D = 225 + 350 = 575\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify all horizontal forces acting on the car of mass $m = 900\text{ kg}$:
- Forward driving force from the engine: $D$.
- Opposing resistance to motion: $R = 350\text{ N}$.

Step 2: Apply Newton's second law in the direction of motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$D - R = ma$$
$$D - 350 = 900(0.25)$$
$$D - 350 = 225$$
$$D = 350 + 225 = 575\text{ N}$$

hints: Use the instantaneous power formula relating power, driving force, and speed: $P = D \times v$.
Substitute the driving force $D = 575\text{ N}$ from part (a) and speed $v = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Multiply $575$ by $15$ to calculate the engine power in watts or kilowatts.
walkthrough:
Calculate the power of the engine using $P = D \times v$:
$$P = 575 \times 15 = 8625\text{ W} = 8.625\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Use the relationship between power, driving force, and velocity:
$$P = D \times v$$
From part (a), the driving force is $D = 575\text{ N}$, and the speed at this instant is $v = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Step 2: Multiply the values:
$$P = 575 \times 15 = 8625\text{ W} = 8.625\text{ kW}$$
